visual_description: The image displays a logo for the "Healthy Brain Initiative" with the subtitle "Road Map for Indian Country." On the left side of the logo is a blue graphic of a human brain viewed from above, showing both hemispheres. The text "HEALTHY BRAIN" appears in large, bold, blue capital letters on the top line, with "INITIATIVE" directly below it in slightly smaller blue capitals. Beneath that, the phrase "Road Map for Indian Country" is written in a smaller, dark blue serif font. The entire composition is set against a white background.

The image displays the logo of the National Council of Urban Indian Health. The design features a circular emblem with stylized figures representing people and urban structures in blue against a white background. Text encircles the central graphic, reading "NATIONAL COUNCIL OF URBAN INDIAN HEALTH." No charts, tables, axes, or numerical data are present.

plain_text:
Educate and Empower Community Members Strategies
Benefit(s) for Each StrategyLow DifficultyModerate DifficultyGreater DifficultyLife Course
1. Work with community members to understand brain health, early warning signs of dementia, and benefits of early detection for persons living with dementia and their caregivers.
Helping Tribal members take steps to promote brain health, reduce stigmas and myths about dementia, and seek early diagnosis of dementia requires clear and consistent messages delivered by trusted sources.• Disseminate health education materials from reliable partner organizations such as NCUIH in various locations throughout the health center and other high traffic areas• Engage with other Tribes and Native organizations at the local, regional, and national level in educational efforts• Integrate brain health education into new or existing curricula; provide in-person or virtual trainings, classes, support groups• Disseminate health education materials about risk and protective factors of dementia at family planning appointments, during diabetes prevention classes, tobacco cessation events, and traditional practices or ceremonies
Adding brain health to other efforts to prevent and manage chronic disease has been an effective public health strategy in states and local areas. Tailoring this approach for AI/AN cultures could have far-reaching impact.• Reach out to your Title VI team to identify resources available to your community• Provide education on brain health at existing community events such as pow wows and health fairs• Create public awareness campaigns on the importance of early detection and ways individuals can reduce their risk of cognitive decline
• Add resources to your webpage (see list of resources on page 13)• Add resources to your webpage (see list of resources on page 13)• Utilize media outlets for public service announcements• Plan education initiatives — consider training of staff, community health representatives (CHRs), local influential people• Train other non-health professionals (educators, childcare educators, business owners, gym or fitness center staff) to recognize the warning signs of dementia and create a referral network
